final_assessment: Seven rules decided by Sal, each with its Mechanism entry; no open questions. D-dl-1: records are written for a reader who knows only what architect decided (raised by Sal from the AI's own jargon). D-dl-2: three records, one job each (ledger entry, stop record, resolution); stop conditions 1-2 begin as a ledger entry that finds nothing to rely on. D-dl-3: a ledger entry cites what it relies on and orbit checks the citation exists; resolutions become precedent. D-dl-4: a fixed list of eighteen areas decides what goes in the ledger, no catch-all test. D-dl-5: records go through orbit emit into the history beside the work. D-dl-6: D-dl-1 is held by record structure plus a reading step in review. D-dl-7: everything is recorded in every mode; a stop halts only when a setting says so.

residuals.kind: a prose field a later stage adds to a record, or a new surface that renders record prose to the user
residuals.method: when a field or surface is added, ask whether its text reaches the user; if it does, it joins this table

residuals.kind: an approved source a ledger entry relies on that is not one of these kinds
residuals.method: such a citation is refused at write, which surfaces the kind; adding it is a change to the requirement

residuals.kind: a judgement that affects the end user or involves security and falls in none of the eighteen areas
residuals.method: G4's closing review classifies a run's changes against the list; a qualifying call in no area adds its area, as a change to the requirement
